messages.content: How do I package produce for market?

Packaging is not decoration. Grading produce into uniform sizes and packing it cleanly gets a better price for exactly the same crop, because buyers pay for predictability and reject lots they must sort themselves. It also reduces damage in transit, so more of what you grew arrives saleable.
Is there any way to deal with armyworm without buying chemicals?

Yes, and on a small plot it is often the better economics.

1. Handpick larvae out of the whorls. Done thoroughly over several days on a small field this genuinely works.
2. Destroy badly damaged plants that will not recover rather than nursing them along.
3. Intercrop so the stand is not a uniform block of maize.
4. Leave the natural enemies alone. Broad sprays kill the wasps and predators that were suppressing the pest for free.
5. After harvest, destroy crop residues, because the pest overwinters in them.

The residue step is the one most farmers skip and it is the one that reduces pressure next season.
Why does it matter how I decide which fertiliser to buy?

Buying fertiliser without testing is the most common way smallholders waste money. You pay for nutrients the soil already has while the one nutrient actually limiting your yield stays short, so the crop does not improve and the fertiliser gets blamed. A test costs far less than a season of the wrong input. Your extension officer will know where testing is available.
What is the right way to start keeping rabbits?

Rabbits suit very small capital: they breed quickly, eat forage rather than competing with the household for grain, and need little space. The failure point is housing. Hutches must stay dry and well ventilated but out of direct sun and rain, because rabbits tolerate cold far better than heat or damp.
How do I plant maize?

Moisture stress at tasselling and silking causes the largest yield loss of any stage.

1. 75cm between rows and 25cm within rows, one plant per stand, about 53,000 plants per hectare.
2. Split nitrogen: a basal compound fertiliser at planting, then top dress with urea at about 3 to 4 weeks, and again at knee height on poor soils. Place fertiliser in a band beside the plant, not broadcast, to cut losses.

If what you see in the field does not match this, take a sample to an extension officer rather than guessing.

Why does it matter how I keep farm records?

Write down what you spent, planted, applied and sold, with dates. Without records you cannot tell which of your decisions made money and which quietly lost it, so you repeat both. A simple notebook is enough, and after two seasons it is worth more than any general advice, including this. Conditions differ between zones and soils, so treat this as a starting point.
I am not sure when to put my sweet potato in the ground. Any guidance?

Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. Lift carefully. Bruised and cut roots rot quickly in storage and do not sell. Keep a note of what you did and when, because next season that record beats any general advice.

I want to start beekeeping. What should I know?

Site hives away from paths, livestock and homes, with shade and water within reach, because bees that must fly far for water work less and defend more. Harvest leaves enough honey for the colony to hold through the dearth period, and a colony stripped bare will abscond. Beekeeping fits well beside cropping, since the same bees improve pollination on nearby fields.
I am not sure when to put my yam in the ground. Any guidance?

Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. Milk harvest of the first tuber can be taken while the plant continues, or a single harvest at senescence. Cure tubers in shade before storing in a ventilated barn. Damaged tubers rot and spread rot to the rest. Your local extension officer can confirm which varieties and products are registered in your area.
My goats have fever, runny nose and mouth sores and several are sick. What is this?

Fever with nasal discharge, mouth sores and rapid spread through the flock points at peste des petits ruminants. Act today, it moves fast and kills young stock hardest.

Separate visibly sick animals and handle the healthy ones first. Stop all movement in and out, so no selling, lending or buying while this is running. Contact your veterinary or extension officer today.

Vaccination is the real control and it has to be in place beforehand.
My maize is not yielding like my neighbour's. What should I change?

1. Moisture stress at tasselling and silking causes the largest yield loss of any stage.
2. 75cm between rows and 25cm within rows, one plant per stand, about 53,000 plants per hectare.
3. Split nitrogen: a basal compound fertiliser at planting, then top dress with urea at about 3 to 4 weeks, and again at knee height on poor soils. Place fertiliser in a band beside the plant, not broadcast, to cut losses.
4. Hybrid seed yields more but must be bought fresh each season. Open pollinated varieties can be saved for 2 to 3 seasons with careful selection, which suits farmers with tight cash.
5. Follows a legume such as cowpea or soybean well, which reduces nitrogen cost.
How is plantain and banana grown?
Plantain and banana are staples of West and Central African smallholder systems, known locally as ogede (Yoruba).

My fowl dey die anyhow. Plenty don die for two days and some neck don twist.

This one serious. Fowl wey dey die sharp sharp with neck wey twist na Newcastle disease. Do something today, e dey move fast.

1. Separate the fowl wey still strong from the sick one now now. Touch the healthy one first before you touch sick one.
2. No sell, no give, no carry new fowl enter. Stop all movement.
3. No leave the dead one where other animal go reach. Ask vet or extension officer wetin be the correct way to dispose am for your area.
4. Call vet or extension officer today make dem know say e dey your area.

No medicine dey wey go cure am once e don enter. Na vaccination be the control, and e must dey before the sickness come. When you restock, follow the vaccination time table, and any new fowl make e stay alone first before e join the others.
What do I need to get right when planting yam?

1. Seed yam of about 250 to 300g, or setts produced by the minisett technique, which multiplies planting material from a single tuber.
2. Large mounds or ridges for drainage and tuber expansion. Compacted soil produces short, forked tubers.
3. Staking lifts the vine into the light and raises yield materially over unstaked yam.

I want to get tomatoes to market without losses. What should I know?

Most tomato loss happens between the field and the market, not in the field. Rigid crates instead of raffia baskets sharply reduce bruising, because baskets crush the fruit at the bottom under the weight above. Harvest in the cool of the morning, keep the fruit shaded while it waits, and handle it once rather than repeatedly. Keep a note of what you did and when, because next season that record beats any general advice.
How do I control maize streak?
1. Tolerant varieties and avoiding very late or staggered planting near infected stands. There is no cure for an infected plant.

Which crops suit the sudan zone?

Single season, roughly 500 to 1000mm. Sorghum, millet, cowpea, groundnut, some maize with fertiliser. Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake.
What is the right way to establish a oil palm field?

1. About 9m triangular spacing, roughly 143 palms per hectare. Crowded palms shade each other and yield falls.
2. Plant tenera hybrid seedlings from a reputable source. Dura palms grown from random seed give much thicker shells and less oil.
What usually goes wrong with soybean?

On soybean a short list of causes covers most of what goes wrong.

What to look for:
- Check for pod shattering at late harvest.
- Check for rust.
- Check for poor nodulation without inoculant.

Match the symptom to the cause before spending money. The wrong treatment costs cash and loses the window for the right one.

Packaging is not decoration. Grading produce into uniform sizes and packing it cleanly gets a better price for exactly the same crop, because buyers pay for predictability and reject lots they must sort themselves. It also reduces damage in transit, so more of what you grew arrives saleable.
How do I stock a catfish pond?

Stocking rate and water quality are one decision, not two. Overstocking raises ammonia, stresses the fish and stunts growth no matter how well you feed. Fish gulping at the surface is a warning that the water cannot carry the load. Either exchange water more often or reduce the number of fish; feeding harder into bad water only makes it worse.
What goes wrong when farmers do not use cover crops between seasons?

A cover crop over the off season protects the soil surface, adds organic matter and smothers weeds before they seed. Bare ground between seasons is a loss you do not see until yields drift down over several years. A legume cover adds nitrogen as well, which makes it close to free.

What grows well in guinea conditions?

Long single season, roughly 1000 to 1400mm. The maize, yam, soybean and rice belt. Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake.

How I go know say my maize don dry reach to store?

Maize wey feel dry for afternoon sun fit still wet too much for inside. Na the outside dey dry first, the inside dey hold water.

Wetin you fit do to check:

1. Bite the grain. If e hard well well and e crack sharp, e don near dry. If e soft or e dey bend, e never ready.
2. Pour some inside empty tin. Dry grain dey make sharp sound; wet one dey sound dull.
3. If co-operative near you get moisture meter, na the correct way to check.

Make you dry am for tarpaulin or raised platform, no be for bare ground. Ground dey push water back enter the grain and dey add sand wey buyer no go like.
I farm in the humid forest zone. What should I be growing?

High rainfall with two seasons. Cassava, plantain, cocoa, oil palm, vegetables. Disease pressure is high because humidity is high. Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake.
What should I focus on to improve my oil palm?

About 9m triangular spacing, roughly 143 palms per hectare. Crowded palms shade each other and yield falls. Harvest on ripeness judged by loose fruit on the ground, not by a fixed calendar. Underripe bunches give less oil, overripe raises free fatty acid and lowers quality. Plant tenera hybrid seedlings from a reputable source. Dura palms grown from random seed give much thicker shells and less oil.
That sounds expensive. What if I cannot afford it?

About 9m triangular spacing, roughly 143 palms per hectare. Crowded palms shade each other and yield falls. Harvest on ripeness judged by loose fruit on the ground, not by a fixed calendar. Underripe bunches give less oil, overripe raises free fatty acid and lowers quality. The unpaid work usually beats the bought input: clean planting material, correct spacing, and weeding on time.

How I go keep my maize make weevil no chop am?

Two thing dey decide am, and the first one na the one people dey skip.

1. Dry am well first. If the maize never dry reach, nothing you do after go work. Maize wey feel dry for afternoon sun fit still wet too much for storage. Dry am for tarpaulin or raised platform, no be for bare ground, because ground go put water and sand back inside.

2. Use hermetic bag like PICS. The bag dey block air so the weevil no fit breathe, and you no need chemical at all. But e only work if you tie the inside liner well every single time you open am. If you leave am loose, na ordinary bag be dat.

Check the store sometimes. If you see hole for the grain or dust for under the bag, weevil don enter.
Any advice on how to sell through a cooperative?

Selling as a group opens buyers who will not deal in small quantities, and spreads the cost of transport, storage and testing across members. It also gives some negotiating position, which an individual smallholder arriving alone at a market does not have. The gain is usually larger than any agronomic change available in the same season.
How do I control stem borers?
1. Destroy or plough in crop residues after harvest to break the carryover, since larvae overwinter in stalks. Early uniform planting across a community reduces pressure for everyone.
There is a small purple flowered weed growing near my maize stems and the maize is yellow and stunted. What is it?

That is striga, also called witchweed. A flowering weed at the base of the stem is not an insect problem, so do not treat it as armyworm.

Striga attaches to the maize root and draws from it, which is why the maize yellows far more than the small weed above ground would explain. It thrives where nitrogen and organic matter are depleted, so it is a soil fertility problem wearing a weed's clothing.

Pull it before it flowers. Each plant that flowers sheds very many long-lived seeds.
Can I just spray something to cure cassava mosaic?

Farmers often spray insecticide expecting a cure. It does not reverse infection. The main control is clean planting material and resistant varieties. Rogue out badly affected plants. There is no spray that cures an infected plant.

What is the right timing for sweet potato?

Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. Lift carefully. Bruised and cut roots rot quickly in storage and do not sell. Conditions differ between zones and soils, so treat this as a starting point.
I want to apply fertiliser so it is not wasted. What should I know?

Place fertiliser in a band beside the plant rather than broadcasting it across the field. Broadcast urea on hot dry ground loses a large share to the air before the plant ever takes it up, so you pay for nitrogen the crop never sees. Placement makes a small quantity work like a larger one, which matters most when cash is short.
What goes wrong when farmers do not use poultry manure safely?

Poultry manure is strong and fast acting, which cuts both ways. Fresh manure burns young plants and carries weed seed, so compost or age it before use. Applied well ahead of planting and worked in, it feeds the crop and builds organic matter at the same time, which bagged fertiliser does not do.

My maize get hole for leaf and I dey see like sawdust for inside the middle. Wetin be dis?

Na fall armyworm be dat. The sawdust wey you dey see na the caterpillar poo, and if e pack for inside the whorl, e clear say na am.

Make you check first:

1. Open the middle of plenty plants, for early morning or evening time when dem dey active.
2. Look for white mark like Y for the caterpillar head.
3. Look four black dot wey stand like square near the tail.

If you see am, start with the thing wey no go cost you money. Pick the caterpillar comot with hand if the farm small. After you harvest, clear the stalks and plough them in, or destroy them as your local guidance advises, because na there the pest dey hide reach next season.

If you wan spray, use product wey dem register for fall armyworm for maize, and follow the rate wey dey for the label. Pour the spray enter the middle of the plant, no be on top leaf, because na inside the caterpillar dey.
What goes wrong when farmers do not protect a sloping field from erosion?

On sloping land, ridge along the contour rather than up and down. Ridges running downhill become channels that concentrate water, and a channel becomes a gully within a season or two. Once a gully forms it takes far more work to repair than the ridging would have cost. Keeping the surface covered, with mulch or a cover crop, protects it from rain impact.

Sweet potato is a staple of West and Central African smallholder systems. Lift carefully. Bruised and cut roots rot quickly in storage and do not sell.

What is the right way to deal with stem borers on maize, sorghum, rice?
1. Destroy or plough in crop residues after harvest to break the carryover, since larvae overwinter in stalks. Early uniform planting across a community reduces pressure for everyone.
I have half a hectare and almost no money this season. What is the single best thing I can do for my maize?

Weed on time. If you can only do one thing, that is the one.

Weeding costs labour rather than cash, and on a small maize plot it changes yield more than any input you could buy with the money you do not have. Maize is most vulnerable to competition in its first few weeks, so weeding early matters far more than weeding often.

After that, in order of how much they give back per naira spent:

1. Correct spacing and one plant per stand, which costs nothing but attention at planting.
2. Planting on established rains rather than the first shower, which avoids a replant.
3. If any cash exists, a small amount of nitrogen placed beside the plant at about three to four weeks, rather than broadcast. Placement makes a small quantity work like a larger one.

Avoid spending scarce money on spraying unless you have actually scouted and found a problem worth treating.
What goes wrong when farmers do not avoid selling into the harvest glut?

Everyone harvests at the same time and prices fall exactly when your crop is ready. Storing well, so quality holds, or aggregating through a co-operative so you can reach buyers who will not deal in small lots, is usually the largest single price gain available to a smallholder. Selling at the farm gate on the day of harvest is the most expensive habit in smallholder farming. Keep a note of what you did and when, because next season that record beats any general advice.

My cassava leaf dey yellow and e twist. I don spray insecticide but nothing change.

Make you stop to spend money for spray. Na cassava mosaic disease be dat, and no insecticide fit cure am.

Na virus. Whitefly dey carry am, but the main way e dey enter na through the stem wey you plant. If you cut your stem from plant wey get the sickness, the farm don carry am before e even germinate. Na why the spray no do anything.

Wetin you go do:

1. This season own don happen. Comot the plant wey bad well well.
2. This one important: no ever cut planting stem from plant wey dey show this sign. Cut from healthy strong plant, from the middle of stem wey don reach eight to twelve months.
3. Try get improved variety like TME 419 or TMS 30572 wey fit resist am.

Clean planting material na the whole control.

What is the right way to establish a cassava field?

Weed control in the first 3 months determines yield more than any other single factor, because cassava canopies late and cannot compete early.

1. Stem cuttings 20 to 25cm long with at least 5 nodes, taken from the middle of mature stems 8 to 12 months old. Never cut from a plant showing mosaic symptoms.
2. Ridges or mounds on heavy or waterlogged soil to prevent root rot. Flat planting is acceptable on free-draining sandy loam.
3. 1m by 1m for sole crop, about 10,000 plants per hectare. Wider at 1m by 1.5m when intercropping with maize.
4. Plant at an angle or upright with two thirds of the cutting buried, buds pointing up.
Just tell me how many millilitres of insecticide per litre of water for armyworm.

I will not give you a number, and I want to be clear about why rather than seem unhelpful.

The correct rate depends on the specific product in your hand. Two bottles on the same shelf can differ several times over in concentration. A number from me could mean you underdose and waste the spray, or overdose and harm yourself, the crop and whoever eats it.

The rate is printed on the label of the product you bought. Use that. If the label is missing or you cannot read it, your extension officer or the agro-dealer who sold it can tell you.

What I can tell you is where to put it: direct the spray down into the whorl where the larvae actually sit. A spray passed over the top of the leaves mostly misses them, whatever the rate.
I farm in the derived zone. What should I be growing?

Transition zone, in places two peaks of rain, supporting an early and a late crop. Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. Your local extension officer can confirm which varieties and products are registered in your area.
How do I get a better crop of pepper?

Space for airflow and keep fruit off the soil to cut fungal losses. Pick regularly once fruit colours. Leaving ripe fruit on the plant slows further setting. Raise seedlings in a protected nursery and transplant when they are sturdy. Direct sowing gives an uneven stand.
Sorry, what does that mean exactly?

Space for airflow and keep fruit off the soil to cut fungal losses. Pick regularly once fruit colours. Leaving ripe fruit on the plant slows further setting. In plain terms, find the source, deal with that, and start with what costs nothing.

Sorghum and millet are staples of West and Central African smallholder systems, known locally as dawa (sorghum, Hausa), gero (millet, Hausa).
Something is wrong with my pepper and I cannot tell what. What should I check?

On pepper a short list of causes covers most of what goes wrong.

What to look for:
- Check for anthracnose.
- Check for aphids and mites.
- Check for blossom drop in extreme heat.

Match the symptom to the cause before spending money. The wrong treatment costs cash and loses the window for the right one. Keep a note of what you did and when, because next season that record beats any general advice.

- Check for rodent damage to young palms.
- Check for poor drainage.

What is the market price of maize in Kano this week?

I do not know, and I will not guess at it. Prices move week to week and by market, and a number invented by me could cost you real money at the point of sale.

For a current price, ask traders at the market itself, other farmers who sold recently, or a local farmers' association, which often tracks it.

What I can say generally is that prices are at their lowest right at harvest when everyone sells at once. If you can dry properly and store well, or sell through a cooperative that aggregates, that is usually where the gain is.

Any advice on how to avoid aflatoxin in groundnut and maize?

Aflatoxin is a mould toxin, worst in groundnut and maize, produced when drying is slow or storage is damp. It is invisible at levels that still cause harm, it does not go away once formed, and it gets consignments rejected by any buyer who tests. The defences are practical: lift and dry fast, never let a drying crop get rained on, and sort out every shrivelled, discoloured or mouldy nut before storage.

How do I deal with soil that stays poor despite fertiliser?

Persistently poor growth despite good rainfall and fertiliser can mean the soil is too acid for the crop to use what you applied. Lime corrects it but works slowly, so it must go on well ahead of planting rather than at sowing. This is worth testing for rather than guessing, because liming soil that does not need it wastes money and can lock up other nutrients. Do the cheapest thing on this list first and give it two weeks before spending more.
